name: Seba
title: Son of Cush
summary: Seba was the eldest son of Cush, who was the son of Ham, Noah's son. He is known as the ancestor of a people and a region in Africa, likely linked to ancient Ethiopia or the Upper Egypt area. Seba is mentioned in the Bible's genealogies and in prophetic texts that speak of distant nations.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Table of Nations
keyEvents.description: Seba is listed as the firstborn son of Cush in the post-flood genealogy, which describes the origin of the world's nations.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Seba's genealogy is repeated in 1 Chronicles as part of the great genealogy from Adam onward.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's Prophecy about Distant Peoples
keyEvents.description: Isaiah prophesies that people from Seba will come to the God of Israel, pointing toward a future turning of distant nations.

keyEvents.title: Nations as Ransom
keyEvents.description: God declares that he has given Egypt, Cush, and Seba as ransom for Israel, showing God's love for his people.

keyEvents.title: The People of Seba Bring Gifts
keyEvents.description: In the book of Psalms it is mentioned that kings from Seba will bring gifts, which prophetically points to universal worship of God.
